steps.say: Not every vomiter of blood needs a hospital bed, and two scores sort them at the door. A Blatchford of zero walks home with an urgent clinic slot, while a Rockall past five after scoping means intensive care and a high risk of dying. Scoring first stops both dangerous discharges and wasteful admissions.
steps.tx: **Glasgow-Blatchford** (pre-endoscopy discharge score) hitting **0** sends upper GI bleeders home with urgent follow-up, while **Rockall** (post-endoscopy mortality score) over **5** predicts death and intensive care need after endoscopy. Scores triage disposition before the scope, saving beds and lives every day.

steps.say: An ulcer that bleeds through two endoscopic attempts has beaten the scope, and the next call is to radiology, not theatre. Coils into the feeding artery stop most gastroduodenal bleeders without an incision. Surgery waits for collapsing patients and failed embolisation, when the duodenum must be opened and the vessel tied.
steps.tx: **Refractory bleeding** (ulcer bleeding past two endoscopic attempts) goes to catheter **gastroduodenal embolisation** (coiling the feeding artery) after **2** endoscopic attempts, with the knife kept back for instability or failed embolisation. Coils first suit high-risk surgical candidates best in every unit today.

steps.say: One tiny vessel can empty the stomach of blood without any ulcer at all. A calibre persistent artery pokes through a pinpoint hole and erupts painlessly into massive vomiting of blood. Clips placed through the scope seal most, and the few that rebleed are stitched through an open stomach.
steps.tx: **Dieulafoy** lesion (oversized submucosal artery) with **calibre-persistent artery** (wide vessel to the surface) and pinpoint mucosal defect unleashes massive painless haematemesis, stopped by endoscopic clipping with surgical oversewing for failures. The vessel always dwarfs the tiny defect completely. Rebleeds get tattooed for the surgeon.

vis.alt: Endoscopic view of brisk arterial bleeding from a Dieulafoy lesion.
vis.caption: A pinpoint defect hides a calibre-persistent bleeder. Credit: డా. గన్నవరపు నరసింహమూర్తి.

steps.say: A patient with an old aortic graft who vomits blood once and then stops is sounding the deadliest alarm in surgery. That herald bleed means the graft has eaten into the bowel, and the next bleed is exsanguination. Scopes waste the window, so the scanner comes first and then the graft comes out with a bypass routed far from infection.
steps.tx: **Aortoenteric fistula** (aortic graft eroding into duodenum) after aortic graft with **herald bleed** (warning bleed) ahead of exsanguination demands urgent CT angiography with graft excision and extra-anatomic bypass. Endoscopy must not delay scanning when graft history exists in any bleeder ever.

steps.say: Bleeding from the twenty feet between stomach and colon hides from both scopes, so the camera goes inside a pill. Capsule endoscopy is photographing the whole small bowel and marks where to dive next. The long double balloon scope follows to burn angioectasias or cut out small tumours, in one or two sittings.
steps.tx: Obscure bleeding with negative endoscopy gets **capsule endoscopy** (swallowed camera mapping the small bowel) next, then **double-balloon enteroscopy** (deep scope with therapy channel) for burning angioectasias or cutting out small bowel tumours. The capsule maps the target first every time without fail.

vis.alt: Endoscopic view of gastric antral vascular ectasia with radiating red stripes.
vis.caption: Angioectasias found by capsule are burnt at enteroscopy. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Painless black stools in a child point down, not up. A Meckel diverticulum lined with stomach tissue ulcerates the ileum across from it and bleeds silently. A technetium scan lights up the ectopic stomach lining, and the operation removes the diverticulum with the ulcerated patch opposite.
steps.tx: **Meckel bleeding** (ectopic gastric mucosa ulcer) in children with **painless melena** (black tarry stools without pain) goes for technetium scan then segmental resection taking in the ulcerated ileum opposite the diverticulum. Ectopic gastric mucosa is the acid source in every such child.

steps.say: Bleeding from below behaves differently when the patient is unstable. Dye spilling from a vessel on CT at half a millilitre per minute points the radiologist straight to it for coiling. Stable diverticular bleeding usually stops by itself, four out of five settling without any procedure. Instability with a blush is an order to embolise now.
steps.tx: Lower GI bleed with instability and **CT extravasation** (dye leaking from the vessel) over **0.5** mL per minute goes to **embolisation** (catheter coiling), while stable diverticular bleeds usually stop on their own four times in five. The blush localises the vessel for targeted coils.

steps.say: When litres have gone in and no source can be found, the whole colon may have to come out to save a life. Past six units without a target, with washout and a scope inside the open bowel still blind, total colectomy with an ileostomy ends the bleeding at the cost of the colon. Segmental guesses in the dark simply rebleed.
steps.tx: **Total colectomy** (removing the entire colon) stands as the final option for unlocalised massive lower bleeding needing transfusion past **6** units, once **on-table colonoscopy** (scope inside the open washed bowel) with lavage fails to find the source. Blind segmental resection rebleeds.
